ratings.text:
No hidden aim,
open at the heart.
ratings.reasons: 14 and 18 characters (line 2 at the limit), 7 words. Line 2 now fits the centre of the picture, where the two yin lines part. But the two lines say the same thing twice: 'no hidden aim' and 'open at the heart' both mean 'nothing concealed', so the lesson has one idea and no second half. The picture's other move, lines 2 and 5 brightening (剛得中, which Wang Bi reads as 直而正, straight and upright), gets no words, and 中孚 is about being trusted, not only about being open. 'Open at the heart' also leans toward emotional openness or self-help, which is softer than the Confucian reading of sincerity backed by reliability. Two verbless phrases describe a person rather than ask something of the viewer. Rewrite: line 1 is the open centre (line 1 of 61, 有它不燕: having another aim brings no peace; Wang Bi 柔在內則靜而順, 物无巧競); line 2 is the firm lines holding each centre, the plain meaning of 孚: be someone whose word holds. 15 and 15 characters, 6 words, imperative like 24 and 44, and a semicolon instead of the colon used by 11, 12 and 27.
ratings.rewrite:
Hold no agenda;
keep your word.
